chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Driving to Omaha, writing for Nat Towles, losing the car
summary: Smith took his wife home to Omaha and Sioux City to write for Nat Towles, but his car was repossessed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Why did you go to Sioux City or Omaha? Why didn't you go back to Kansas City?

Well, that was my wife's home. See, I didn't have no job. I was taking her home; she had two children there, and her mother was there. So I just went on back there, and said, "Well, I can start arranging for Nat Towles down there in Omaha, so I'll take my car and drive down there and stay two or three days and write some arrangements for him..." And one thing made me come back, because I didn't have no job in either one of those towns, nowhere. And I didn't have the car paid for. I still owed some money on the car. Well, I was trying to get me a job
to pay, and when the man finally come... I got a couple of payments behind, and before I could get the money up, he come and take the car.
He came all the way to Omaha and get it?
Yeah. To Sioux City to take my car away from me. So I got on the bus and come back to Kansas City.
